audit.whatIsWrong: Six rows agreed across layers; phases[6].side read "Skill" while content win[6] and the packet both read Fizz.
audit.why: 54.62% over 1558 games, FAVOURED 4/10. Packet levelChart is Fizz on all seven and content win[0..6] is Fizz on all seven. Only the full layer's 2+ items row dissented, and its own why ("Late Fizz erases one carry per fight") describes Fizz winning.
audit.corrected: phases[6].side set to Fizz. The other six rows were already consistent and were left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text told the reader to jump in "whenever his Q/E are down" — those are 5s and 3.5s abilities that are effectively never down.
audit.why: Overload is a flat 5s and resets off his other casts; Spell Flux is 3.5/3.25/3/2.75/2.5s. The only ability with a real punish window is Rune Prison at 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s. Realm Warp is 180/160/140s and is a roam tool, not lane pressure.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, whys[2] and phases[2].why now key off Rune Prison's 11s instead of Q/E; Realm Warp's 180s written in.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page called the root Ryze's E, and never mentioned the Flux condition that gates it — which is the entire interaction.
audit.why: Riot's Rune Prison (W) text: it traps a target, damaging and SLOWING them, and 'If the target has Flux on it, they are instead rooted.' Spell Flux (E) is the debuff applicator. So the root is conditional: no Flux on you means the 615-range cage is only a slow. That inverts the counterplay — you dodge the orb, not the cage. wants.you[2] and the content early paragraph both named E as the root.
audit.corrected: Written into tldr, winCon, enemyWin, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.early, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[0].d, tradeBad, wants.you[2] and the early paragraph.

audit.why: Rune Prison 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, Spell Flux 3.5s down to 2.5s, Overload flat 5s.
audit.corrected: All three written in, with the point that Spell Flux at 3.5s should be assumed always available.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fizz is repeatedly described as having poke: "your poke already threatens trades", "Your Urchin Strike poke chips him for free".
audit.why: Urchin Strike is a 550-range dash through a target, not a poke tool, and Ryze's Overload is a 1000-range projectile. Fizz does not out-range Ryze; he chips with W-empowered attacks after closing.
audit.corrected: whys[0] and the early paragraph rewritten around W-empowered attacks.

notes:
BIGGEST FIX: the page named the wrong ability as Ryze's root and omitted the condition that gates it. Rune Prison (W) damages and SLOWS; it roots only 'if the target has Flux on it' (Riot's text). Spell Flux (E) is the applicator on a 3.5s cooldown. The page called the root 'his E', which sends the reader watching the wrong cooldown and the wrong cast — and the real rule (do not be standing there with Flux on you) never appeared anywhere.

SECOND FIX: three fields advised jumping in 'whenever his Q/E are down'. Overload is a flat 5s that resets off his other casts and Spell Flux is 3.5s — neither is ever meaningfully down. Rune Prison at 11s is the only window that exists.

THIRD FIX: Fizz was described twice as having poke ('your poke already threatens trades', 'Your Urchin Strike poke chips him for free'). Urchin Strike is a 550-range dash; Overload is a 1000-range projectile. Fizz does not out-range Ryze.

CHART: only one row needed moving — phases[6].side from Skill to Fizz, where content win[6] already reads Fizz on disk (so no content edit is proposed; the target string is already there). The other six rows agreed across both layers and the packet.

UNVERIFIED, not written: whether Playful/Trickster's untargetability removes an existing Flux debuff or merely dodges the cast that would consume it, and whether Chum the Waters' knockup can interrupt the Realm Warp channel.
